# sqlite3 / ossfuzz

sqlite3's own fuzz target `ossfuzz` ([source](source/ossfuzz.c), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over tarball?uuid=trunk (sqlite.org/src/tarball?uuid=trunk release archive c4b300b2).

Runs the fuzzed text as SQL through sqlite3_exec() on an in-memory database with a progress-handler time cutoff, VDBE-op/LIKE/length limits, a 20 MB heap limit and an authorizer that denies vdbe_*/parser_trace pragmas; result rows are only formatted with sqlite3_mprintf and freed; every return code (open, complete, exec, close) is ignored.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against tarball?uuid=trunk from the release archive c4b300b2.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source differs from the upstream file at the pinned commit; the copy in source/ is the file as built.
- This copy of the harness could not be matched to an upstream file at a pinned commit, so it is marked modified; it is the file as built.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch sqlite3` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `ossfuzz.plain` | 1,005,656 | `ac4c933f746a5697c7e9523896cb3d2002a33327fa19547ab0330cb3622c563e` |
| ubsan | `ossfuzz.ubsan` | 1,203,104 | `796f72809f12685c1abe0f1deeb9f557771275646f76162e6c103f66f2ab587c` |
| asan | `ossfuzz.asan` | 3,169,656 | `cce7abf5fdd4c83bc05d44067f19c4c2c5a462c535145f17cb35405ac4256fb3` |
| asan-ubsan | `ossfuzz.asan-ubsan` | 3,184,568 | `5a867c8c4bc21ac78ec564217af6dc0c35091b7dce1444883fb1a0cd79d36df5` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
